MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  FEBRUARY 28, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:08 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Deputy City Attorney Kane Thuyen
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Associate Planner Kelley Thom

Others Present:  Jeff Romanelli, Park and Activities Commission
  Tim Zigrang, Planning Commission

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The following Brownie/Girl Scout Troop 185 led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance:
Cornerstone Smartie Cats, Cornerstone Cute Dolphins, Cornerstone Courageous
Cougars, Cornerstone Daisy Dolphins and Cornerstone Cute Pandas.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 14, 2017

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 14, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  PRESENTATION BY COX COMMUNICATIONS

  Kristen Camuglia, Government Affairs Manager, Cox Communications, provided
  an overview of the company’s history and highlighted the new products they are
  offering, i.e. increased internet speed, program enhancements, etc. She noted
  that the state franchise will begin a 10-year term on April 27, 2017.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked Ms. Camuglia for attending the meeting and
  invited her to come back more often in an attempt to engage the community
  and allow them to have a voice in the process.

  Ms. Camuglia commented that Cox is committed to the community and that
  she is available if there are any issues or problems.

B.  Sandra Valeri, PVP PTA, Vice President, Legislation and Advocacy, requested
  the Council to consider and support a Social Host Ordinance to hold adults
  accountable for allowing underage drinking parties in their home. She further
  noted that it is their desire for all the Peninsula cities to adopt this ordinance.
  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that it is a good idea to coordinate this
  ordinance with the other Peninsula cities.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that this item will be discussed at the Policy
  Development Session.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 20-16; APPLICANT:  JUDY CHAI; LOCATION:
  5883 CREST ROAD

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the public hearing on the
  project approvals (Ordinance and Resolutions); 2) Take public testimony; 3)
  Discuss the issues; 4) Approve for introduction Ordinance No. 713, amending
  the zoning designation of 5883 Crest Road from Commercial Limited (C-L) to
  Medium Density Residential (RA-10); 5) Approve Resolution Nos. 2389, 2390
  and 2391; and 6) Continue the public hearing to the next available City
  Council meeting for second reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 713.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 28, 2017
   Associate Planner Thom provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF commended everyone involved for reaching a
  satisfactory conclusion to this project.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Planning Director Wahba provided
  background on how this project ultimately became two homes instead of four.
  He noted that the Applicant believed this would be the most feasible plan.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN regarding the shared driveway,
  Planning Director Wahba noted that there will be an easement between the
  property owners.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired if there was any discussion about
  installing porous concrete for the driveway. Planning Director Wahba noted
  that there was not, but perhaps pavers could be utilized. COUNCILMAN
  ZUCKERMAN asked the Applicant to consider this option.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  Gary Maxwell, Architect, thanked the staff, Planning Commission and COUNCIL
  for their patience and provided a brief history of how the two single residences
  came to fruition for this property. He noted their preference would have been
  for two driveways, but it was problematic to work around the flood control
  channel, and therefore, ended up with a common driveway.

  Helen Cannefax, President, Seaview Villas Homeowners’ Association,
  commented that they have been closely involved and gained support from all
  their property owners. She was also pleased to note that the Applicant has
  addressed everyone’s concerns.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that she has been involved with this project
  when she served on the Planning Commission and appreciated the Applicant’s
  cooperation and thanked Planning Director Wahba and the Planning staff for
  their creative and innovative work.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL also commended the Planning Commission for
  the time they spent and thanked everyone for their patience.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted his appreciation for the Applicant’s patience
  as well. He then asked if language could be provided for future owners to avoid
  litigation in the event a problem should arise with the shared driveway.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, MAYOR ZERUNYAN stated that if a
  problem should occur, it would be a private matter between the property
  owners.

  Judy Chai, Applicant, provided a history of this property and commented that
  her intention is to pay it forward by donating some of her proceeds to her
  personal causes. She thanked the Seaview Homeowners’ Villas, Mr. Maxwell,
  and in particular, Associate Planner Thom and Planning Director Wahba for
  their assistance.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO INTRODUCE ORDINANCE 713 AMENDING THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES ZONING MAP – REZONING FROM COMMERCIAL LIMITED
  DISTRICT TO MEDIUM DENSITY RESIDENTIAL DISTRICT FOR FIRST
  READING.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Assistant City Manager Grammer read Ordinance No. 713 by title only.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 28, 2017
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2389 ADOPTING AN INITIAL
  STUDY/MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION AND A MITIGATION
  MONITORING AND REPORTING PROGRAM FOR TENTATIVE PARCEL
  MAP NO. 74599—A TWO LOT SUBDIVISION, CONSISTING OF A 0.244-
  ACRE PARCEL (PARCEL 1), AND A 0.269-ACRE PARCEL (PARCEL 2)
  WITH  A  GENERAL  PLAN  AMENDMENT  ZONE  CHANGE,
  NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY DETERMINATION AND GRADING
  PERMIT, FOR THE NEW CONSTRUCTION OF TWO, TWO-STORY
  SINGLE FAMILY HOMES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Assistant City Manager Grammer read Resolution No. 2389 by title only.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2390 AMENDING THE LAND USE
  ELEMENT OF THE GENERAL PLAN RELATED TO PA-20-16 –
  CHANGING THE LAND USE DESIGNATION FROM NEIGHBORHOOD
  COMMERCIAL TO MEDIUM DENSITY RESIDENTIAL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Assistant City Manager Grammer read Resolution No. 2390 by title only.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2391 APPROVING TENTATIVE PARCEL
  MAP NO. 74599 FOR A TWO-LOT SUBDIVISION, CONSISTING OF A
  0.51-ACRE PARCEL WITH A NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY
  DETERMINATION  AND  GRADING  PERMIT  FOR  THE  NEW
  CONSTRUCTION OF TWO, TWO-STORY SINGLE FAMILY HOMES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Assistant City Manager Grammer read Resolution No. 2391 by title only.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING TO THE NEXT REGULAR
  COUNCIL MEETING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 21, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 21, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF
  FEBRUARY 21, 2017 - SPECIAL EVENT PROPOSAL

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the addition of a movie night
  to the City's special event offerings for FY 2017-18.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 28, 2017
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE ADDITION OF A MOVIE NIGHT TO THE CITY'S
  SPECIAL EVENT OFFERINGS FOR FY 2017-18.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 11-16; APPLICANT: ROLLING HILLS COVENANT
  CHURCH; LOCATION: 2221 AND 2222 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve PA-11-16, including the
  associated License Agreement, all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF inquired about the lighting for the sign. Planning
  Director Wahba explained why the lighting was changed and that the intent of
  the Planning Commission was to have the sign itself illuminated rather than the
  base. He further noted that the Planning Commission decided that the sign
  should be moved further back from the street. MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF stated
  that motorists driving by may not see the sign at that location.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN inquired where else illuminated signs are located.
  Planning Director Wahba noted that there are several lighted signs throughout
  the City and is not uncommon.

  Planning Director Wahba went on to explain that the sign would be in the right-
  of-way.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted her concern as Palos Verdes Drive North is a
  very busy street, and the need for a visible sign would be necessary because the
  Church provides many activities.

  Susan Johnson, Ministry Services Director, Rolling Hills Covenant Church,
  noted that they have received positive input from the COUNCIL and Planning
  Director Wahba and are looking to have a welcoming entrance to the City. She
  brought material samples they intend to use to construct the sign and noted
  that, while the colors match their buildings, they are open to minor
  modifications.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired if there was a desire to move the sign
  closer to the street. Ms. Johnson responded that if it did not interfere with the
  flood drain, it would be fine.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer inquired if the Traffic Engineer reviewed this
  project. Planning Director Wahba noted that she did and approved the location.
  He then noted that if there is a desire to move the sign closer, he will work with
  the Traffic Engineer.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that it would be the Applicant’s choice if they wish to
  move the sign closer to the street.

  Bob Alley, Operations Director, Rolling Hills Covenant Church, noted that the
  sign is 18 inches from the three-rail fence and could move it five more feet and
  not impede anyone’s vision.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that the lighter colors would be more visible than the
  darker colors.

  Mr. Alley noted that the north side sign is also lit and preferred to have it
  remain.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL commented that she likes the signs either way
  and preferred to leave the decision of colors up to the Applicant.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 28, 2017
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE PA-11-16 LEAVING THE CHOICE OF COLORS UP TO THE
  APPLICANT, INCLUDING THE ASSOCIATED LICENSE AGREEMENT, TO
  THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

D.  PROPOSALS FOR PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR 2017
  STREET RESURFACING PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the agreement and proposal
  from HR Green to provide professional engineering services for design, bidding
  assistance, construction management and observation services and materials
  testing for the 2017 Resurfacing Project in the amount of $122,394.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ inquired as to why the reimbursable expenses
  were not included in the main cost.  Assistant City Manager Grammer
  explained that this would be a separate cost which would include printing, bid
  packets, advertising, etc.

  In response to an inquiry, Mike Myers, HR Green, explained the difference
  between a project manager being the “eyes of the project” and the construction
  observation as “boots on the ground.”

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted that she attended a Montecillo Homeowners’
  Association meeting and questioned the removal of their street from the list of
  improvements. She noted that the slurry seal project was held back because of
  the Butcher development, and now that it is coming to a close, they are being
  asked to wait another two to three years before the road is repaired. In the
  meantime, she asked if the street could be slurry sealed, and once the Cal
  Water Project is completed, repave the road.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer responded that a “fog seal” and asphalt paint
  could be performed to improve the aesthetics of the street until the resurfacing
  takes place a few years later.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ inquired if slurry seal is worth the effort because it
  was not satisfactorily done in their neighborhood.

  Mr. Myers explained the slurry seal process noting that it typically prolongs the
  life of a street by five to seven years and brings it to a uniform color, but is not a
  remedy for the condition of the street if it needs major rehabilitation.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE AGREEMENT AND PROPOSAL FROM HR GREEN TO
  PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR DESIGN,
  BIDDING  ASSISTANCE,  CONSTRUCTION  MANAGEMENT  AND
  OBSERVATION SERVICES AND MATERIALS TESTING FOR THE 2017
  RESURFACING PROJECT IN THE AMOUNT OF $122,394.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SANCON ENGINEERING CONTRACT AMENDMENT - STORM DRAIN HEAVY
  CLEANING AND VIDEO INSPECTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council amend the contract with Sancon
  Engineering, Inc., subject to review and approval by the City Attorney, to
  provide a supplemental scope of services for heavy cleaning, condition
  assessment and closed circuit television (CCTV) inspection on the remaining 25
  high priority storm drain pipes in an amount not to exceed $168,750.

FEBRUARY 28, 2017
   Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO  APPROVE AMENDING  THE  CONTRACT  WITH  SANCON
  ENGINEERING, INC., TO PROVIDE A SUPPLEMENTAL SCOPE OF
  SERVICES FOR HEAVY CLEANING, CONDITION ASSESSMENT AND
  CLOSED CIRCUIT TELEVISION (CCTV) INSPECTION ON THE
  REMAINING 25 HIGH PRIORITY STORM DRAIN PIPES IN AN AMOUNT
  NOT TO EXCEED $168,750.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  RESOLUTION NO. 2392 - SUPPORTING MEASURE H

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES SUPPORTING MEASURE H - A COUNTYWIDE MEASURE TO
  PREVENT AND COMBAT HOMELESSNESS TO BE HELD IN LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY ON MARCH 7, 2017.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2392.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Assistant City Manager Grammer read Resolution No. 2392 by title only.

C.  SALARY SURVEY

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the revised proposal from
  Management Partners to conduct Phase II (salary survey) of the City's salary
  administration study.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Assistant to the City Manager
  Davis noted that assessment of comparator cities, development of the template,
  etc., are included in the $16,000 cost.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis noted that the data collected by staff will be
  incorporated into the templates that Management Partners’ creates.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted her concern regarding ending up in a situation
  such as when the economic downtown occurred and preferred setting a new
  model in terms of having salaries address the pension obligation. She further
  noted that much of the data is already in place and questioned whether this
  cost needs to be spent on analyzing data and utilizing the same cities that were
  considered in the past.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that perhaps this item needs more
  discussion. He then noted his reluctance to have staff undertake the survey,
  but would like to explore how this would work, i.e. averages, salary ranges.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis noted that she would gather the
  information and the consultant would then analyze the data. She further noted
  that a discussion could take place with the consultant and report back to the
  COUNCIL.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN reiterated that the City has attracted and retained
  good employees without a substantial turnover.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ commented she would like to know the direct
  effect of the analysis and how it would be presented.
